newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 27.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The banking council of the Czech National Bank (CNB) cancelled the fluctuation band for the crown. The governer of the CNB, Josef Tosovsky announced yesderday that the currency basket is also cancelled, and a deciding factor in the currency policy is the relation of the crown to the German mark. According to the first remarks from traders, the crown should fluctuate around 10 to 15 percent below the mid-point of the former fixing basket.

- The trade deficit for April amounted to 15.3 billion crowns, the largest monthly deficit so far this year. For the first third of this year, there was an increase in imports by 11.2 percent and exports by 6.3 percent year-on-year.
- The largest domestic freight forwarding company, Chechofracht Praha, ended with losses for the first time last year of 72.3 million crowns with revenue of 3.82 billion.

- Omnipol a.s, the largest domestic weapons trader, had an increase in turnover last year by nearly nine percent to 2.55 billion crowns. Gross profits increased by more than 100 million to 380 million, and net profits tripled to 16 million.
- According to audited results, Ceska Posta had gross profits of 565 million crowns last year and after-tax profits of 461 million crowns.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - In a general meeting of shareholders of Komercni Banka yesterday, it was decided that Richard Salzmann will remain the general director of the bank.
- Shareholders of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka decided yesterday to not pay out dividends from last year's profits but to add to its reserve funds.
- Shareholders of IPB bank will decide today which of the candidates for the state's stake in the bank will be given a detailed summary of the bank's accounts.
- Diesel, formerly Skoda Diesel, was made bankrupt yesterday according to a ruling from a commercial court in Prague.
- Stock analysts expect resuscitation of the capital market after the central bank's decision to cancel the fluctuation band.

PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel understands the sense of the central bank's exchange measures and strongly believes that the necessity to carry them through will lead the cabinet to quickly propose a principally political, not only a cosmetic solution for the current situation.
- The new terminal at Ruzyne airport in Prague, on which construction began in 1995, will open on June 3.

- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka changed its rates yesterday. Its new Prime rate is now 23 percent, interest on one-year and two-year credits is now 21 percent, and for credits for two years and longer, the rate is now 19 percent. This is an decrease of all rates by two percent.
- Sales of Skoda automobiles in CEFTA countries increased by 29 percent to 13,012 vehicles, making Skoda the second most-sold brand after Fiat.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Yesterday's talks on restructuring the cabinet did not lead to a decision. The only sure thing is that the head of the Civic Democratic Alliance, Michael Zantovsky will not take a seat in the Foreign Ministry or the Defence Ministry.
- The leader of the Social Democrats, Milos Zeman, said yesterday that the entire cabinet should resign.
- President Vaclav Havel invited the three ministers that announced they will leave the cabinet to Prague Castle to find out their reasons for leaving.

- Galaxie, which is the third commercial television station with a nationwide licence after Nova and Prima, began broadcasting in Prague yesterday. Galaxie can be received in only about 70,000 households that have cable television in Prague.
